Branch.d: A separate line of work in a git repository, so changes can be made without disturbing the main version until they're ready.

Commit.d: A saved snapshot of changes in git, with a message explaining what changed. Commits can be inspected and undone.

Diff.d: The exact lines added and removed between two versions of files. Reviewing diffs is how you check what changed.

Merge conflict.d: What happens when two branches changed the same lines differently and git can't decide which version to keep; a person must choose.

Rebase.d: A git operation that replays your commits on top of another branch for a tidier history. It rewrites those commits, so it's unsafe on branches others use.

Force push.d: Pushing with git's --force option, which overwrites the remote branch's history. Dangerous on shared branches because it can erase others' work.

GitHub CLI.d: GitHub's official command-line tool, gh, for working with pull requests, issues and CI runs from the terminal.

Pull request.d: A request to merge one branch into another on GitHub, where teammates review the diff, discuss it and run checks before it's accepted.
